said a phase 3 trial of Tezspire (tezepelumab) in eosinophilic esophagitis found that the TSLP blocker led to histologic remission in most patients and reduced dysphagia (difficulty swallowing) symptoms.

The CROSSING trial examined Tezspire 210 mg and 420 mg given subcutaneously every four weeks. At week 24, 64.8% and 68.9% of patients given, respectively, the 210 mg dose and 420 mg dose, achieved histologic remission vs. 3.5% of those on placebo.
The biologic also reduced the frequency and severity of dysphagia symptoms by, respectively, 18.8 points and 22 points from baseline vs. 14.7 points for placebo.
